validity.recommendation: Reclassify as a CRUDE OIL feeder line (move to GOIT / Fuel=Oil), not a gas transmission pipeline; the physical pipe is real but mis-typed as gas.
validity.researcher_notes: The pipe physically EXISTS (not a phantom), but GEM's Fuel=Gas classification is not supported by any independent source and appears wrong. GEM's own cited sources are all about the Al-Ahdab OIL field (BBC Arabic 2011 on Ahdab oil production start; Iraq Business News Ahdab field page; OPEC ASB 2017 p.134) — none describes a GAS pipeline. Independent sources uniformly describe the Al-Ahdab -> Zubaidiya feeder as a CRUDE OIL pipeline: (1) Al-Sharq (Iraqi press quoting the State Company for Oil Projects/SCOP) calls the project 'مشروع مد أنبوب النفط الخام المغذي لمحطة كهرباء الزبيدية – الأحدب' (the crude-oil feeder pipeline for Zubaidiya power station), completed at 76 km, delivered via two crude-oil pumping stations at Al-Ahdab and a receiving station at Zubaidiya. (2) MEES (2023) states Zubaidiya is an 'oil-fired power plant' supplied with crude oil (e.g. 24,000 b/d from Gharaf), not gas. (3) China.org.cn (Arabic, CNPC BRI feature) says the Al-Ahdab project 'يوفر الوقود لمحطة كهرباء الزبيدية' (supplies fuel to Zubaidiya, Iraq's largest power plant). The Al-Ahdab field's associated gas is processed to LPG for domestic distribution in Wasit, not piped as fuel gas to the plant. Endpoints (Al-Ahdab field -> Al-Zubaydia, Wasit), owner (Iraq Ministry of Oil), and FuelSource=Al-Ahdab all fit a crude line. Conclusion: real pipe, but it is a crude-oil power-station feeder mislabeled as a gas transmission trunk. Tier high: >=2 independent origins (SCOP/Iraqi press, MEES, China.org.cn) agree it is crude-oil / an oil-fired plant.

validity.recommendation: Correct length: real line is ~75-76 km (~47 mi). GEM's LengthKnown=73 with units 'mi' (=117 km) is almost certainly a km/mi units error (73 was meant as km, close to the sourced 75-76 km).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists LengthKnown=73.00 mi (= ~117 km). Independent sources give the built Al-Ahdab -> Zubaidiya feeder as 76 km (Al-Sharq / SCOP: 'مد الأنبوب بطول 76 كم') and ~75 km (English trade-press descriptions of the same project). The GEM figure of 73 matches 75-76 km far better as KILOMETRES than as miles, so the 'mi' unit tag is likely wrong (should be ~75-76 km / ~47 mi). Flagging as a spec/units conflict rather than silently passing. Diameter (16 in) and Capacity (blank) could not be independently corroborated and are moot pending the reclassification to a crude line.

routes.start_name: Al-Ahdab (Al-Ahdeb) oil field, Wasit province (~27 km west of Kut, ~180 km SE of Baghdad)
routes.corridor_desc: Runs entirely within Wasit province, NW from the Al-Ahdab oil field (Al-Ahrar/Al-Ahdeb area west of Kut) to the Zubaidiya thermal power station north of Kut. Straight-line separation between the two sourced points is ~65 km, consistent with a routed ~75-76 km pipeline. Corridor bound is moderately tight (both endpoints are named, sourced facilities within one province) but the intermediate alignment is unsourced, so treat as a corridor, not a traced route. Note: the built line uses two crude pump stations at Al-Ahdab and a receiving station at Zubaidiya.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from sourced named facilities: Al-Ahdab field centroid ~32.424N,45.714E (field bounding box 45°30'-45°46'E / 32°23'-32°35'N per remote-sensing lit; ~27 km west of Kut per Arabic press); Zubaidiya power plant ~32.7736N,45.0826E (published plant coordinate). Coordinates are approximate facility points, not surveyed pipe vertices; no coordinates were invented. Al-Sharq/SCOP names the crude pump stations at Al-Ahdab and the receiving station at Zubaidiya; those station points are not individually geolocated so no waypoint coords are asserted.

summary: P4067 is a real pipe but MISCLASSIFIED: it is the Al-Ahdab->Zubaidiya CRUDE-OIL power-station feeder (~75-76 km, oil-fired plant, SCOP), not a gas transmission line; also a length/units conflict (73 'mi' vs sourced ~76 km).
